input.quote: 9.3 Customer may terminate an Order Form immediately if Vendor suffers a material Security Incident, repeatedly misses a critical service level, violates Applicable Law in performing the Services, or infringes a third party's intellectual property and cannot provide the remedies required by Section 20.5.
input.rationale:
Section 9 provides only for-cause exits (9.1 material breach, 9.2 insolvency, 9.3 specific Vendor failures) and 9.5 confirms cumulative remedies; a search of the document returns no termination-for-convenience provision for either Party. The term is three years (8.1) and Section 2.1 imposes a USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay commitment "without reduction or termination rights", so Customer has no convenience exit in a multi-year term — walk-away territory under the rule. Section 8.2 non-renewal and Section 27.3 force-majeure termination are partial exits only and are not substitutes. Vendor has no convenience right, so no deletion is needed; we insert a new 9.4 giving Customer the preferred 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, expressly overriding Section 2.1, and confirming Vendor may not terminate for convenience during a term.</rationale>
<parameter name="confidence">0.88

ops.text: 9.4 Notwithstanding Section 2.1, Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, without penalty or early-termination fee, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination. Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or an Order Form for convenience during a term.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added a Customer right to terminate for convenience on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, as our playbook requires for any term longer than 12 months; Section 9 currently offers only for-cause exits and Section 2.1 negates termination rights across a three-year commitment. If helpful, we can discuss 60 days' notice as a fallback.
proposal.summary: Insert Customer termination-for-convenience right (30 days' notice, pro-rata refund) and confirm Vendor has no convenience right during a term.
